fields.explore_cta: Build My Black Friday Landing Page
fields.features_heading: What Sits Behind a Black Friday Sale Page
fields.features_subheading: Shoppers see a price and a button. These six parts handle what happens after someone presses it.
fields.feature_1:
A countdown to the hour the deal ends

Give the end time and time zone, such as Monday at 11:59 PM PT. Emergent builds the countdown into the page, and at zero the offer block switches to the message you wrote.
fields.feature_2:
Early access signups in a table you own

Each early access signup saves to a database you own, with the email, the time, and the link that brought the visitor. Read the list by hour, or export it before the sale opens.
fields.feature_3:
A stock count that drops as visitors reserve

Set the number of units for a doorbuster. The page shows how many units are left, updates with each reservation, and swaps the Reserve button for a waitlist form at zero.
fields.feature_4:
One discount code per email address

Load a batch of codes from your checkout. The app gives each email address one code, saves the pair in a codes table, and shows the same code if that address asks again.
fields.feature_5:
Signups sent on to HubSpot or Slack

Built apps connect to any tool with an API, so a signup can join a HubSpot list as it lands. A rule you write, such as 50 or more seats, sends a Slack or email alert to one person.
fields.feature_6:
Back next November with a new offer

Keep the page on your own domain, which is included and uses credits, and change the offer by prompt each year. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Black Friday Landing Page Examples
fields.tab_content_1:
1,284 subscribers in line before the sale opens

Ferncastle Candle Co. lets its list shop Black Friday a day early. The early access page asks for an email and a favorite scent, and 1,284 people have signed up so far. Each signup joins a HubSpot list named BF Early Access, and the store sends that list the sale link on Thursday at 6 PM ET.
fields.tab_content_2:
163 skillets claimed and 37 left to reserve

Halverline Cookware has 200 cast-iron skillets at $39 for pickup at its store on Black Friday. The page takes one reservation per email and shows the count beside the Reserve button. After 163 reservations, it reads 37 left. When the count reaches zero, the button turns into a waitlist form.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each email address gets its own single-use code

Every email address that reaches Brightmoss Outdoor Supply's page gets one code for 25% off, good from Friday through Cyber Monday. Teodora Vance entered her email and got BF25-K7QM. The code is saved in the codes table next to her address. If she asks again, the page shows her the same code.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any request of 50 or more seats goes to a rep

Quillmark sells project tracking software and takes 30% off annual plans through Cyber Monday. The offer page asks each team for its company name and seat count. Corbel Logistics asked for 84 seats, and because 50 or more seats go to a person, Ines Varga got a Slack direct message.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Black Friday Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a Black Friday landing page around one offer and a firm end time, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose one offer for the page
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the start and end times
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Show the regular price you charged
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the single deal the page sells, such as 30% off annual plans or a $39 skillet, and put that price or discount in the headline. Shoppers decide in seconds. A page with one offer reads faster than a grid of twelve.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the hour the sale opens and the hour it ends, and name the time zone, such as 9 AM ET on Friday. Use the same times in every email and ad that links to the page, and set the countdown to the end time.
fields.howto_step_3_des: If you put a was price next to the sale price, use the price you listed the item at before the sale. The FTC's pricing guide looks for the actual, bona fide price at which the article was offered to the public on a regular basis.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give your list a head start, such as 24 hours, and say on the signup form when the early link arrives. Ask only for the email and one field you will use later, like a favorite product or a store location.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the offer and its times into one prompt, along with the signup rule. Emergent builds the page with its countdown and the table behind it. Prompt again to change any part, such as the message shoppers see once the sale ends.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Set the end time 10 minutes out and sign up three times, once with a repeated email. Watch the countdown reach zero and the offer block change. Then put back the real end time and delete the test rows.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish a couple of weeks before the sale and link to the page from your homepage. Early access signups need those days to build. After Cyber Monday, point the offer block at the next sale instead of taking the page down.

faq_plan.q: What is a black friday landing page?
faq_plan.a: A Black Friday landing page is a single page built for one sale on Black Friday, the Friday after Thanksgiving in the United States. It names the offer, shows when the offer ends, and asks the shopper for one action, such as reserving an item or claiming a code.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a black friday landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write down the offer and its end time, then pick the one thing a shopper does on the page. Describe those in a prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder, and it writes the page, including a countdown and a table for every signup. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What do good Black Friday landing page examples have in common?
faq_plan.a: Good Black Friday landing page examples put one offer in the headline, state the end time with its time zone, and ask for one action. The four examples above follow that pattern: early access for subscribers, a skillet reservation, a single-use code, and an annual plan request.

faq_plan.q: How early should Black Friday landing pages go live?
faq_plan.a: Put Black Friday landing pages live two weeks or more before the sale when they collect early access signups, and a few days ahead when they only show the deal. If the page opens a series of emails and offers, plan it as a sales funnel landing page. The page Emergent builds saves each signup to a database you own from the first day.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a separate Cyber Monday landing page?
faq_plan.a: Not when the offer runs through the weekend. Cyber Monday falls three days after Black Friday. Change the headline and the countdown on the same page instead of sending shoppers to a new URL. Build a separate Cyber Monday landing page when the offer itself changes, such as an online-only deal.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse the same Black Friday landing page every year?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Keep one URL and swap the offer each year instead of publishing a new page for every sale. Google's John Mueller has suggested you use one single URL and reuse that depending on the individual seasons. Links the page earned last November keep pointing at this year's offer.

faq_plan.q: Does a Black Friday landing page work for a software offer?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the offer fits how businesses buy, such as a discount on annual plans instead of a one-day price. Ask for the company name and seat count, and send large requests to a sales rep. For buyers you court all year, a b2b landing page suits the longer sales cycle. Emergent builds the form and the routing rule from one prompt.

faq_plan.q: How do I add a countdown timer to a Black Friday landing page?
faq_plan.a: Give the timer one end time and name its time zone, such as midnight ET on Monday, and place it next to the offer. Decide what the page shows at zero: a sold-out note, the next sale date, or a waitlist form. Emergent builds the timer from the same prompt as the rest of the page.

faq_plan.q: What should a Black Friday landing page say after the sale ends?
faq_plan.a: Say the sale has ended, then give shoppers a next step, such as a restock waitlist or a signup for next year's early access. Leave the page live instead of deleting it. A visitor who arrives from an old link sees a clear message, not an error.

faq_plan.q: What can I offer on a Black Friday landing page besides a discount?
faq_plan.a: Offer something that costs little to give, such as free shipping or a free buying guide. A guide traded for an email works like an ebook landing page and keeps growing your list after the sale ends.

plan.angle: The top 10 is design galleries (Pinterest, Dribbble, Figma, Magnific), template builders (Swipe Pages, ConvertFlow) and example roundups (WiserNotify, MailerLite, Digitorm, Wix). They show how a sale page looks and stop at the banner. This page shows four Black Friday pages doing the work behind the banner: an early access list that fills before the sale opens, a doorbuster with a live count of units left to reserve, a single-use code issued once per email, and a software company's annual plan offer that sends big teams to a sales rep. The FAQ covers what good examples share, when to publish, extending the page to Cyber Monday, reusing one URL each year, honest was-and-now prices, countdown timers, B2B offers and offers other than a discount. Holiday landing page is a sibling and stays out of the headings.
